question.text: A fly’s position relative to a fixed origin $O$ is given by the function $x(t) = \dfrac{t}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{8}\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{8}t\right) \, \textrm{m},$ where $t$ is the time in minutes. Find its average position of the fly between $0$ and $2$ minutes.
question.explanation:
To calculate the average value of the position on $[t_1,t_2],$ we use the average value formula \[ x_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{1}{t_2 - t_1}\, \int_{t_1}^{t_2} x(t) \, \textrm dt. \]

So, we get

\begin{align*} x_{\text{avg}} &= \dfrac {1}{2-0}\, \int_0^2 \left(\dfrac{t}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{8}\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{8}t\right) \right) \textrm dt \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\left. \left( \dfrac{t^2}{4} + \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{8}t\right) \right)\right|_{0}^{2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\left(\dfrac{2^2}{4} + \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{8}\cdot 2\right) \right) - \left( \dfrac{0^2}{4} + \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{8}\cdot 0\right)\right)\right)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\left(1 + \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \right) - \left( 0+1\right)\right)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{4}. \end{align*}

Therefore, the average position is $\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{4} \,\textrm{m}.$

question.text: A golden eagle is moving in a straight line with a velocity of $v(t)=\dfrac{2^t}{12}\,\textrm{m/s},$ where $t$ is the time in seconds. Find the average velocity of the golden eagle on the interval $[2, 6].$
question.explanation:
To calculate the average value of the velocity on $[t_1,t_2],$ we use the average value formula \[ v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{1}{t_2 - t_1}\int_{t_1}^{t_2} v(t) \,\textrm{d}t. \]

So, we get

\begin{align*} v_{\text{avg}} &= \dfrac {1}{6-2}\, \int_2^6 \left(\dfrac{2^t}{12}\right) \textrm dt \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4 \cdot 12 \cdot \ln 2} \left( 2^t \right)\Big|_{2}^{6}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{48\ln 2}\left( 2^6 - 2^2\right)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{60}{48\ln 2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac 5{4\ln 2}. \end{align*}

Therefore, the average velocity is $\dfrac 5{4\ln 2} \,\textrm{m/s}.$

question.text: Find the average acceleration of a particle on the interval $[0,2]$ if its acceleration in $\textrm{mm/s}^2$ is given by the function $a(t) = e^{t} + 2t,$ where $t$ is the time in seconds.
question.explanation:
To calculate the average value of the acceleration on $[t_1,t_2],$ we use the average value formula \[ a_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{1}{t_2 - t_1}\, \int_{t_1}^{t_2} a(t) \, \textrm dt. \]

So, we get

\begin{align*} a_{\text{avg}} &= \dfrac{1}{2-0} \, \int_0^2 \left( e^{t} + 2t\right) \, \textrm dt \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( e^{t} + t^2 \right)\Big|_0^2\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\left(e^2 +2^2\right)-\left(e^0 +0^2\right)\right]\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(e^2 +4-1\right)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(e^2 +3\right). \end{align*}

Therefore, the average acceleration is $\dfrac{1}{2}\left(e^2 +3\right) \, \textrm{mm/s}^2.$

question.text:
A robotic sled moves along a straight track with velocity $v(t) = t^3 - t,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds and $v$ is measured in meters per second.

Find the average acceleration $a_{\text{avg}}$ over the time interval $t \in [1,3].$ Do not round your answer.
question.explanation:
The average acceleration is the average rate of change of the velocity, so

\begin{align*} a_{\text{avg}} &= \frac{v(b)-v(a)}{b-a} \\[6pt] &= \frac{v(3)-v(1)}{3-1} \\[6pt] &= \frac{\left[(3)^3-(3)\right]-\left[(1)^3-(1)\right]}{2} \\[6pt] &= \frac{(27-3)-(1-1)}{2} \\[6pt] &= \frac{24-0}{2} \\[6pt] &= \frac{24}{2} \\[6pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{12}\,\textrm{m/s}^2. \end{align*}

Therefore, the average acceleration is $12\,\textrm{m/s}^2.$

question.text:
A test cart moves in a straight line with velocity $v(t) = \dfrac{3}{t},$ where $t$ is measured in seconds and $v$ is measured in feet per second.

Find the average acceleration $a_{\text{avg}}$ over the time interval $t \in [1,3].$ Do not round your answer.
question.explanation:
The average acceleration is the average rate of change of the velocity, so

\[ \begin{align*} a_{\text{avg}} &= \frac{v(3)-v(1)}{3-1} \\[6pt] &= \frac{\left[\frac{3}{3}\right]-\left[\frac{3}{1}\right]}{2} \\[6pt] &= \frac{1-3}{2} \\[6pt] &= \frac{-2}{2} \\[6pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-1}\,\textrm{ft/s}^2. \end{align*} \]

Therefore, the average acceleration is ${-1}\,\textrm{ft/s}^2.$
